Flip RUN_WINNERS_CURSE_DIAGNOSTIC_NOW there to True and run that cell to populate this section, then re-run Stage 8 (FORCE_RECOMPUTE_STAGES={'stage8'}) to fold it into this report.

evaluation_design: Single split: search and selection used only its training data and the family was chosen on Stage-3 training-side scores, so the Stage-5 test score is untouched by selection (no CI: n=1).
three_way_role_disclosure: Stage 1-4 are model-SELECTION only (never read test data). Stage 5 is ESTIMATION on the held-out test partition(s) (see evaluation_design for which rows selection could have seen). Stage 7 is DEPLOYMENT: a final refit on more data than any evaluation step used, never itself re-evaluated. corrected_winner_family is chosen on the Stage-3 TRAINING-side scores, never on Stage 5's test scores. Stage 6 (family-vs-family significance testing) is in the DEAD CODE section and does not contribute to this report.
ranking_methodology_note: Both the Stage 4 per-family architecture selection and this corrected_winner_family are chosen by Borda (average-rank) combination of 4 equally-weighted criteria — accuracy, bal_accuracy, macro_f1, kappa (each: higher rank is better) and the train-val gap on those same 4 metrics, clipped at 0 (lower rank is better, i.e. less overfitting) — rather than a raw weighted average or a single-metric argmax. Ranks (not raw metric values) are averaged because these metrics are not on a common scale (kappa is chance-corrected; accuracy is not balanced-class-aware) and are mutually correlated by construction, so naive raw-value averaging would silently overweight whichever metric has the widest spread — a scale-free rank average (a Borda count; Dwork et al. 2001) avoids this. The train-val gap uses in-sample training predictions; it is a deliberate penalty on overfitting, a stated preference rather than a published selection rule. Plain accuracy is included as a 4th ranking criterion (a deliberate choice; it is often left diagnostic-only under class imbalance); the raw metrics are kept verbatim in stage3_cross_split_scores/stage5_test_scores, so this choice is auditable against the un-ranked raw metric regardless.
cost_control_note: Stage 1/3's chain-CV candidate scoring shares one node-fit cache per (context, seed) [Stage 1] or per split [Stage 3] across every candidate scored in that sweep, since StratifiedKFold's fold boundaries depend only on (labels, n_splits, seed) — never on a candidate's config — so two candidates that happen to share an identical router/branch/gate/subgate/nonblazar_router config get that fit only once; this changes nothing about what is fit or scored. Separately, when REDUCE_STAGE3_CANDIDATES=True (see stage3_shortlist_reduction above), Stage 3 only re-scores the top STAGE3_SHORTLIST_TOP_K of Stage 1's already-Borda-ranked shortlist per family, rather than the full shortlist — a breadth trim on top of already-ranked candidates, not a change to any combo-grid width, repeat count, or fold count.
